newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal to replace TAP medium haul fleet.
newsitem.headline: Portugal to replace TAP medium haul fleet.

text.p: The Portuguese government will announce on Friday the winner of a competition to provide a new medium haul fleet for state airline TAP-Air Portugal, a spokesman said.
The bidders are Boeing Co and European plane consortium Airbus Industrie, which hope to supply 22 new medium haul planes to TAP.

"The decision about the acquisition of new planes for TAP belongs exclusively to Planning and Public Works Minister Joao Cravinho and will be announced at a news conference on Friday," the Planning and Public Works Ministry spokesman said.
A source in TAP said new leasing agreements should bring savings to the Portuguese government.
"The new fleet will permit annual financial savings of around four billion escudos," the source said.
The total value of the deal was not known.

With the arrival of the new planes, some of the present leasing contracts will be cancelled and replaced by 16-18 new leasing contracts, under which TAP will eventually own the planes, and four to six operational leasing contracts.
TAP now operates 30 operational leasing contracts covering its fleet of 30 medium haul aircraft.
Under the plan, the new planes will be delivered between 1998 and 2001, the TAP source said.
The board of TAP was due to hand to Cravinho today a report containing an opinion on the best option to take, the source added.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
